title: Cross-stitch bluebell border
subtitle: A repeating bluebell and leaf border on 28-count white evenweave
excerpt: A repeating bluebell and stem border pattern that can be sized to fit any rectangular frame. The base repeat unit is 30 by 20 stitches; four repeats along the long sides and two on the short sides give a finished frame of approximately 25 by 18 cm on 28-count evenweave. The design suits a sampler border, a tray cloth edge, or a picture frame mat.
sourceNotes: Original design. The bluebell (Hyacinthoides non-scripta) is native to Britain and Ireland and a protected wildflower. Repeating border patterns are a core format in British cross-stitch tradition.

content.text: A repeating border requires exact counting. Stitch a single repeat unit from the chart, count the repeats needed for your chosen frame size, and then work outward from the centre of each side. Starting from the centre of each side rather than from a corner means any counting error is absorbed symmetrically at the corners rather than showing at one end.

items.label: Fabric
items.value: 28-count white evenweave, sized to your frame plus 8 cm border for mounting

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 340 (medium blue-violet), 341 (light blue-violet), 3746 (dark blue-violet), 3809 (very dark teal), 319 (very dark pistachio), 320 (medium pistachio), 368 (light pistachio), 3865 (white)

content.text: Measure your frame opening and convert to stitches: frame opening in centimetres divided by 0.7 gives the approximate stitch count at 14-count equivalent (28-count over two threads). Round to the nearest multiple of 30 for the long sides and 20 for the short sides. Add one corner motif at each corner; the corner occupies a 20 × 20 stitch square.
Start with one corner to establish the border position on the fabric. The corner uses a turning bluebell stem with a bell cluster facing inward.
Work the first long side outward from centre.

Find the midpoint of the long side and begin the first repeat there. Work repeats outward to each corner. The repeat unit: an upright bluebell stem with two or three bells and paired leaves on each side.
Stitch the opposite long side, then the two short sides. Work each remaining corner to close the border rectangle.
Add back-stitch stem lines and bell details.
Outline the bluebell bells in 3746 using one strand. Work the drooping bell opening in a small curved back-stitch arc in 3865.
Press face-down on a towel. Lace or fold-back mount into a picture frame. The bordered fabric works well with a monogram or date added to the interior later.
